text:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing a slow NVMe degradation in the eu-west2-ephemeral pool. Multiple kubelet attach failures and checksum mismatch logs; 12 failed GPU attaches in last 10m. Impact: pod scheduling delays and a handful of preemptible requeues.

maria: :eyes: any logs you can paste?

alex: paste: `kubelet: attach failed: nvme: read error checksum mismatch on /dev/nvme0n1 (gnode-455)`

ops-bot: ALERT io_high_latency eu-west2-ephemeral avg_iops=185000 threshold=150000 window=5m :fire:

tai: Could be janitor/scrub overlap with heavy batch launches. Can we run SMART and cordon candidate nodes?

alex: Running smartctl on gnode-455:
```
SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: PASSED
ID# ATTRIBUTE_NAME          VALUE  RAW
  5 Reallocated_Sector_Ct     98
  9 Power_On_Hours          12345
 197 Current_Pending_Sector  14
```

maria: Reallocated sectors 98 + pending 14 = bitrot/firmware issue territory. We should cordon+drain affected hosts to stop risking pod corruption.

tai: Commands: `kubectl cordon gnode-455 && kubectl drain gnode-455 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

jin: Are cleaner/scrub jobs thrashing disks right now? I saw a scrub backlog earlier this morning that could increase write amplification. If janitor is scanning the same set while batch traffic spikes, it will amplify IOPS.

alex: Good catch — scrub cadence overlapped a large GPU batch window 03:00-04:00 UTC. I started cordoning gnode-455/458/463. fsck on gnode-455 shows broken superblocks on a couple partitions — copying logs to /tmp for SRE. Vendor ticket opened (TKT-1109).

maria: Immediate mitigation options:
- throttle janitor/scrub for eu-west2-ephemeral for 6h
- route new GPU allocation requests to fallback pool in eu-central2 or us-west2 until eu-west2 stabilizes
Note: routing cross-region will increase egress and reserved capacity mismatch costs (~+$$/hr, estimate in ops-budget).

ops-bot: runbook: https://runbook.internal/redwood/ephemeral-nvme (linked)

sre-oncall: For capacity: set cluster allocator constraint to prefer us-west2 for new preemptible GPU launches; keep allocation_ratio=0.8 to preserve headroom.

jin: To throttle janitor: `./ops janitor throttle --pool eu-west2-ephemeral --rate 0.2` (reduces scrub concurrency).

alex: I've applied a temporary ConfigMap change to disable nightly deep-scrub for eu-west2 and flagged the three nodes for expedited replacement. Patch snippet applied: `apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  scrub.enabled: "false"
`

maria: I'll spin up 2 reserved GPU instances in eu-central2 for 2 hours (on-call approve?) to absorb critical rollout traffic while we replace unhealthy nodes. That keeps user-facing latency stable.

sre-oncall: Approved. Also adding alert: checksum_errors > 5 in 10m -> high severity.

alex: Action items:
- cordon/drain gnode-455/458/463 (in progress)
- run full fsck and snapshot affected volumes
- escalate vendor ticket with SMART data and logs
- throttle janitor for eu-west2 (jin)
- route non-critical GPU alloc to fallback pool (maria)
- add dashboard widgets for checksum_errors and reallocated sector counts (maria/sre-oncall)

ops-bot: SUMMARY: 3 nodes cordoned, janitor throttle requested, vendor ticket TKT-1109 opened, fallback capacity requested.

maria: I'll post a short blameless postmortem template after we stabilize and capture cost delta.

sre-oncall: If any node hits Reallocated_Sector_Ct > 100 or Pending > 50, mark for immediate retirement and replacement.

alex: continuing work now, will keep thread updates.
